item.title: Opinion: Internet for all, built for Alaska - Peninsula Clarion
item.description: For too long, high-speed internet — something most Americans take for granted — has been a luxury in many Alaska communities. Entire regions have been left grappling with slow, unreliable, or prohibitively expensive service. In a state where distance and geography define daily life, connectivity is not just about convenience – it’s about opportunity.

item.title: Opinion: Is it time deep-six the Jones Act? - Peninsula Clarion
item.description: In 1920, over a hundred years ago, Congress passed the Merchant Marine Act. The legislation mandated that persons or goods that are transported between any United States ports must be carried in vessels built in the United States and owned and crewed by U.S. citizens. Today, Alaska is dependent on the few U.S.-built ships carrying supplies from Washington state to Alaska. The cruise ship fleet cannot carry passengers from one port of Alaska to another. item.title: Minister’s Message: Bright and vivid reasons - Peninsula Clarion
item.description: Sunrises and sunsets are beautiful in the winter months. I say winter because I don’t usually see them during the summer; they are too early and too late. I don’t often see the sun begin and end its journey across the sky in the summer unless I’m going fishing or coming home from a fishing trip.

item.title: Opinion: Why Alaska should pass CSSB 64 - Peninsula Clarion
item.description: For nearly a decade, election policy in Alaska has been defined more by debate than results. Over the past ten years, the Legislature has introduced 164 election-related bills and more than 40 resolutions, yet only three measures became law, and none significantly changed how Alaska conducts elections.
